text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions. Variable and function names should describe what they do, so others can follow the logic quickly. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and change. Clean code is also easier to maintain over time. When problems appear, developers can find and fix them faster. In short, readable code saves time and reduces mistakes for the whole team.
